focus.title: LiteLLM AI gateways: CISA adds sandbox escape CVE-2026-40217 to its exploited list (Nov 18), on top of the unauthenticated RCE chain CVE-2026-42271 + Starlette CVE-2026-48710 seen in honeypots
focus.why: CISA put CVE-2026-40217 in KEV (federal deadline Dec 2). In LiteLLM 1.81.8-1.83.9 the custom-code guardrail test endpoint (POST /guardrails/test_custom_code) escapes its sandbox, so anyone with an admin/master key, including a leaked or default one like sk-1234, gets root in the default Docker image; a public exploit has existed since April. Separately, LiteLLM 1.74.2-1.83.6 plus Starlette before 1.0.1 allows an unauthenticated RCE chain through the MCP test endpoint, which SANS honeypots saw being sprayed from Nov 16. Gateways hold OpenAI, Anthropic and cloud keys, which ARTEX-style agents hunt. Overnight X posts say financially motivated actors are exploiting LiteLLM RCE (unverified detail on which CVE). Corgea (Nov 19): the Google LLMjacking evidence behind the KEV listing actually describes a /key/regenerate rebind (no CVE, fixed in 1.84.0) that turns a leaked inference key into admin; chained with the sandbox escape it gives root.
focus.action: Upgrade LiteLLM to 1.84.0 or later (covers both; at minimum 1.83.11 for CVE-2026-40217) and Starlette to 1.0.1+. Block /guardrails/test_custom_code and /mcp-rest/ at the reverse proxy, never use a default master key, and keep admin routes off the internet. If requests to those endpoints appear in logs, rebuild the proxy and rotate the master key and every provider key it stored (follow LiteLLM's steps if LITELLM_SALT_KEY was unset).
focus.ai_note: AI product: LLM gateway that stores AI provider keys; two bugs exploited this week.

news.title: Chinese-nexus actor's Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own
news.blurb: Autonomous Cairn agents told only to 'obtain shell access' found a MONAI Label path traversal and used it for root in September. The operator then pointed them at a second university. Fix merged, release pending.

news.title: BabidiGhost: An AI-Augmented Cybercrime Operation
news.blurb: A jailbroken AI agent did the technical work for an unskilled operator against 50+ European banks, insurers and towns; breaches came from ordinary exposures, and MFA and allowlists stopped it.

news.title: OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms
news.blurb: OpenRouter off-boarded three inference providers and removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention after Dragos's canary study showed prompts stolen from inside AI hosting firms for months. Rotate any secret ever sent in a prompt.

news.title: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices
news.blurb: GL.iNet confirms its GoodCloud remote-management service was abused to install malware and reverse shells on customer routers and KVMs; cloud hole fixed, firmware updates due Nov 22, infected devices need reflashing.

news.title: Cleverbridge warns hackers stole credit card numbers, CVVs in data breach
news.blurb: The payment platform behind many software vendors' web stores found an intrusion Nov 4; attackers copied stored card numbers, expiry dates and CVVs. Notices began Nov 20; scale and affected vendors not disclosed.

news.title: CERT-In flags unauthorised transactions at financial service providers and AI-driven agentic attack frameworks
news.blurb: CERT-In advisory CIAD-2026-0062 (Nov 20): attackers alter payment records and approvals at service providers, and agentic AI frameworks automate recon and exploits across sectors.

news.title: Security event: Prompt leakage for requests in June and July of 2026
news.blurb: An AI coding agent committed a Hugging Face credential to a public repo; an outsider downloaded stored prompt samples and tested credentials found in them.

news.title: Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets
news.blurb: Stolen credentials let attackers create pods and read Kubernetes Secrets in customer clusters on Nov 17; rotate tokens and cluster secrets.

watch: Maileva (La Poste subsidiary, France, reported this week): breach exposed names and addresses of about 22 million people, called one of France's largest. Expect postal/parcel-themed phishing. Source: this.weekinsecurity.com Nov 22 edition (citing DataBreaches.net, Actu.fr, Infosecurity Magazine).

Microsoft Entra Connect Health API flaw (moved from focus; exploited, Nov 21): Microsoft told affected tenants that a flaw in the Entra Connect Health API (introduced Jul 23, found Nov 9) was exploited for read-only access to administrator and technical-contact email addresses, tenant IDs and names, domains, country/region, Entra license tiers, directory-sync status and an expired, unused certificate. Microsoft says no passwords, hashes, tokens, valid keys, AD topology or Az Action: No patch to install (fixed server-side Nov 19). Check for Microsoft's notification, warn admins named as contacts about targeted phishing, make sure privileged accounts use phishing-resistant MFA, review Connect Health settings and Entra audit/sign-in logs; Microsoft's script at aka.ms/ConnectHealth https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-entra-connect-health-flaw-exploited-to-steal-tenant-data/

Jupyter MCP Server CVE-2026-77359 (CVSS 9.3, advisory Nov 20): DNS rebinding lets a malicious website hijack a local Jupyter MCP server; a public PoC was reported Nov 22, no exploitation. Update to 1.0.3. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9x8x-crjq-g64h

Tower Records Japan (notice Nov 21, updated Nov 22): intrusion into Tower Records Online found Nov 19; about 11M records leaked: 10,214,652 login records (email, member ID, password hash), 2.78M member profiles, 776,953 delivery addresses; no card data, store still offline. Change any reused password and expect Tower Records-themed phishing.

KEPCO (Korea Electric Power, Nov 22, Yonhap): attacker stole data from its KEPCO ON customer platform (650,487 users: names, resident registration numbers, bank account and card details, billing) and SRM procurement system (869,761 users); found Nov 20, its second breach in a month.
Zozo (Japan, Nov 20-21): about 15.2M customers' data exposed via the PLAID KARTE marketing-platform breach (also Marui, SMBC, EPOS, MUFG). KARTE customers should check their exposure.

Fullerton Health (Singapore, CNA): a standalone server for its Migrant Worker Primary Care Plan exposed about 140,000 work-pass holder records (names, FIN, DOB, contacts, addresses); no health or financial data.

pnpm CVE-2026-130756 (CVSS 9.8, per X/TheHackerWire Nov 22): an outdated bundled Node runtime trusts the revoked eMudhra CA, enabling TLS interception and package substitution during installs. Upgrade pnpm to 10.34.8 or later.

NTT Docomo (6th notice, Nov 22): the Nov 4 intrusion into Docomo Online Shop and My docomo leaked data of up to about 300,000 customers, now listed as including bank names, branch and account numbers and account holders, plus child-support program data; most My docomo functions are restored. Expect Docomo-themed phishing. https://www.docomo.ne.jp/info/notice/page/261122_00_m.html
Unverified (X, Nov 22): Puppet Enterprise CVE-2026-115731 described as AI-discovered; no confirming source. It is on CISA KEV, so patch regardless.

Chainflip (cross-chain swap protocol, reported Nov 21): about $4.86M (520 ETH, 3.25M USDC, 758K USDT and BTC) drained from its vault with a valid Schnorr signature, likely compromised signing keys; funds laundered via Tornado Cash. No action unless you hold funds in Chainflip vaults; follow its updates.

KodeKloud (training platform, notice Nov 21): attacker exploited a software flaw to get admin access to an internal reporting tool on Nov 10; names, emails, usernames and some job titles accessed, no passwords or payment data. Expect targeted phishing if you have an account.

Java4Shell CVE-2026-114938 (moved from focus; found by AI): OpenJDK pre-auth RCE on x86-64 with AVX-512 VBMI (OpenJDK 17.0.6+, 21, 25, 27); attackers probing, no confirmed break-in. Apply the October/November Java updates.

Prime Intellect (advisory, Nov 2026): an intruder replaced its DeepSeek V4.1 Flash endpoint with a refusal-stripped ('abliterated') model for about 53 hours (Nov 8-10); it reports no prompt or credential exposure.

Ghostscript 'Upload2Shell' CVE-2026-125396 (CVSS 8.5): real bug with a fix, but not on CISA KEV and no exploitation reported; update Ghostscript where uploads are converted. Update (Nov 22): reportedly found with AI by researcher Paulos Yibelo; others say they reproduced a working PoC within minutes of the write-up, so expect exploitation soon.
Rakuten Securities (Japan) says a test environment may have leaked details for up to 4.47M accounts and login IDs for up to 11.25M; passwords and PINs not affected (its Nov 17 notice).
Cisco published an advisory (Nov 21) on which Cisco products are affected by the Nov 18 nginx fixes (nginx2root); check Cisco appliances that embed nginx.
Unverified (single X post): CVE-2024-28545 reportedly exploited on Tenda routers; no vendor or CISA confirmation seen.
ServiceNow CVE-2026-18883 (Nov 21): indirect prompt injection in the Now Assist for CSM email-reply AI agent; fixed centrally by ServiceNow, no action needed, not exploited.

SurrealDB before 4.0.0: capability bypass in the embedded JavaScript engine CVE-2026-134292 (CVSS 9.8), MCP server SQL injection CVE-2026-134293 and several authorization/path-traversal flaws. Upgrade to 4.0.0.
Rclone 1.51.0-1.75.x CVE-2026-134352 (CVSS 9.2): auth bypass in 'serve sftp --auth-proxy'. Upgrade to 1.76.0.

New malicious PyPI packages (OpenSSF, Nov 21): instantscrape 0.1.0/0.1.5/0.1.8 (infostealer on install or import) and signed-manifest-guard 0.1.7 (downloads and runs a remote RAT). Remove and rotate secrets from a clean machine if installed.
Chrome CVE-2026-125350 (XML/libxslt use-after-free, exploited, fixed in 157.0.8103.50): on CISA KEV, due Nov 24; Edge needs the same fix.
BADBOX botnet on cheap Android TV boxes is back (BleepingComputer, Nov 21) with record ad-fraud volume; remove uncertified Android TV boxes from networks.

GnuPG GPGME CVE-2026-129975 (critical double free, Nov 20; The Hacker News Nov 21): a malicious OpenPGP key with a long user ID can corrupt memory in apps that use GPGME before 2.3.1 (most mail clients, many XMPP clients, Samba, Gpg4win); data theft possible, RCE not ruled out; not exploited. Update to GPGME 2.3.1 (legacy 1.24.4), Gpg4win 5.1.2, and rebuild apps that bundle it statically.
Windows AD Domain Services RCE CVE-2026-70229: a public PoC is now on GitHub (per X, Nov 20-21). Confirm domain controllers have the patch.
Restrictions for BuddyPress (WordPress plugin) CVE-2026-120539 (CVSS 9.8, unauthenticated RCE): public exploit released (per X, Nov 21). Update or remove the plugin.
Meta Muse (NebuSec research, Nov 21): a malicious webpage could make the agent leak private chats and memories and escape to root on the user's VM; all exploits patched before publication.
YMCA Singapore (CNA, Nov 21): its Youth For Causes portal database (names, schools, some full or partial NRIC numbers) was breached; found Oct 19, data access neither confirmed nor ruled out.

New malicious packages (OpenSSF, Nov 20-21): npm @pkgship/frps-windows-amd64 0.71.1, aia-b-locator-fe 1.0.3, orion-overlord; PyPI signed-manifest-updater 0.1.5 (runs a remote script on install). Remove and rotate secrets if installed.
Bitcoin Core CVE-2026-117348 (Nov 20; found by Spiral's AI tool Project Loupe): a peer can stall a node by repeating one orphan txid; upgrade to 30.5, 31.3 or 32.1 (29.x is end of life).

Staples Canada (CBC, Nov 20): a third party reached customer data on the staplesprint.ca print site between Nov 1 and Nov 5; Staples says no financial data and no other sites affected. Expect Staples-themed phishing.

phpAfterShell PHP CVE-2026-126714 (found with depthfirst AI): fixed in PHP 8.5.13/8.4.28/8.3.37/8.2.36. Update (Nov 22): X posts claim exploit code is on GitHub (unverified); Cloudflare and CERT Sante report no attacks and it is not on CISA KEV. Patch now.

NGINX2Root (moved from focus; PoCs public, no confirmed exploitation): pre-auth RCE in NGINX with HTTP/2 (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633), found with Wiz's AI scanner. Install F5's fixed NGINX/NGINX Plus builds or disable HTTP/2 until patched.

FBI (NBC/CNN, Nov 20): investigating an apparent breach of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), the system that shares crime records between federal, state and local police. No details yet on the attacker, entry point or data taken; watch for FBI confirmation and CJIS guidance to agencies.
USDA (NBC, Nov 20): employees were told Nov 19 that a system used to pay farmers was breached; officials say no other systems were hit as of Nov 20. Expect payment-themed phishing aimed at farmers.

Qubole / JPMorgan Chase, Visa, Mastercard (moved from focus): n0n used Qubole's AWS credentials (Oct 14-26) to assume IAM roles customers granted Qubole; banks confirm vendor-held marketing data (names, emails; no card data) taken. Remove dormant vendor AWS trust roles, check CloudTrail AssumeRole since Oct 1, expect bank-themed phishing.
F5 BIG-IP (moved from focus; not reported exploited): five critical APM/iRules overflows (CVE-2026-121805 and others) with no workaround; install F5's Nov 18 hotfixes.

JetBrains TeamCity CVE-2026-132891 (CVSS 9.8, per X Nov 21): RCE through external pull requests; update to the fixed releases (2025.11.8 or the 2026.1 fix) and don't build untrusted PRs on privileged agents.
Spring Security CVE-2026-59273 (CVSS 9.8, per X Nov 21): critical flaw when an app binds raw user input, part of Spring's 50-fix November update; update Spring Security.

SMBC (Nov 20): up to 14M records (birth date, age band, gender, notification flags; no names, contacts or account numbers) leaked in the PLAID KARTE breach, on top of MUFG and EPOS Card. KARTE users: rotate connector secrets.

Roll20 (Nov 2026 notice): an image-upload flaw let an attacker reach an account database on Nov 16; under 1% of users had names, emails and bcrypt password hashes (some card last-four) exposed. Change reused passwords.
Palo Alto Networks (Nov 20) published its product-impact advisory for NGINX2Root (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633).

Tigerfish (San Francisco transcription firm used by police, prosecutors and tech companies; TechCrunch Nov 20): a public cloud bucket exposed transcripts, police interview and body-cam media, and invoices. Now secured; customers should ask what was exposed.

Peach Aviation (Japan, per Kyodo Nov 20, not yet confirmed by the airline in our sources): email-delivery contractor Yumil Link was breached in October, and about 9M records (names, emails, addresses, itineraries; no card or passport data) leaked.

EPOS Card (Japan, Nov 20): another victim of the PLAID KARTE marketing-tool breach. Customer IDs and gender for up to about 8.5M records exposed; names, ages, incomes and cash-advance limits for about 60,000. No card numbers. KARTE users: rotate connector secrets.

Infcurion (Japan): attackers broke into its Wallet Station white-label payment-app platform (found Nov 19). Paydon, the app run by Minami-Nippon Bank and three Kagoshima banks, was suspended at 6:20 AM JST Nov 20. Banks say 251,172 users' membership data, payment methods and transaction history leaked.

WhatsApp (Nov 20): CVE-2026-23871 in WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4 could leak a target's IP address via crafted Click-to-WhatsApp ad replies; WhatsApp believes a scammer used it. Update the Android apps.

ruby2shell CVE-2026-132825 (moved from focus; no exploitation reported): Ruby 3.3.14/3.4.13/4.0.10 fix it; as of Nov 19 Veria listed GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server and Chatwoot as not yet patched; public PoC expected in about a week.
Gemini 4 Neon (Google, Nov 20): a cyber-focused version for vetted defenders (Fairwind Program) is coming; Google claims frontier-level bug finding and patching. Expect more AI-found CVEs.
NSA (via SecurityWeek, Nov 20): malware on DoW employees' personal PCs records CAC PINs and uses the card while it stays in the reader to sign into federal sites; remove CACs when not in use.
teahy-znrpz-util (npm, Nov 20): GitHub-flagged malware that runs a hidden payload on require and avoids CI; remove, rebuild and rotate secrets.

SonicWall Gen 6 firewalls (Nov 20): end of security patches, even for critical flaws; SonicWall urges replacement and removal from the internet edge and expects exposed units to be attacked (it cites AI-assisted attacks). Inventory and replace.

Linux KVM CVE-2026-99312 (Terra Security, Nov 20): from root inside a guest VM, researchers read about 127 GB of host memory on DigitalOcean and wrote host kernel memory on AMD hosts with nested virtualization. Intel hosts unaffected; DigitalOcean live-patched. If you run your own AMD KVM hosts, update the kernel (fix merged Nov 2) or disable nested virtualization.

SBC Medical Group (SEC filing, Nov 20): breach of a clinic platform in Japan now affects over 2 million people (1.62M basic records incl. patient card numbers, 255,416 reservation requests, 4,513 treatment descriptions, 14 credit cards); a separate Tribeau reservation-service admin breach hit about 19,000. MOSH (928,617 email addresses) also disclosed Nov 19.

New Zealand Defence Force (RNZ, Nov 20): its website provider reported unauthorised access; the Force4Families Defence Discounts database (names, emails) was accessed and websites were taken offline. Expect phishing.

Frappe (per X, Netlas, Nov 20): an email-endpoint authorization flaw (no CVE yet) lets any authenticated user, even a Website User, send email through the site; reported as actively exploited. Update Frappe/ERPNext and disable self sign-up if not needed.

Kurly (Korea, Nov 20): an attacker stole authentication credentials on Nov 17 and reached internal business systems; 10,699 curator-program members' names, IDs, phone numbers, emails and social handles leaked, some with bank-account and resident or business registration numbers (MoneyToday). https://www.mt.co.kr/en/living/2026/11/20/2026112017320311063

FastUnlock (The Hacker News, Nov 20): unpatched Windows technique lets someone with physical access start programs on a locked PC without signing in (limited account, not admin). No patch yet; keep laptops encrypted and in sight, and watch for Microsoft guidance. https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/new-unpatched-windows-0-day-fastunlock.html

ROMULUS ClickFix delivery service (Blackpoint, Nov 20): fake-fix prompts plus signed-binary sideloading drop a new RAT similar to CNCMachineRMS and Legion Loader. Block users from pasting commands into Run/PowerShell where possible.

Coinone (Korea crypto exchange): support contractor MetaM was breached Nov 12; data customers gave in support chats or calls (incl. passwords, resident numbers, wallet addresses) may be exposed. If you ever told support a password, change it and any reuse.

flyto-core CVE-2026-77312 (AI-agent workflow engine, CVSS 10, unauthenticated file write): upgrade to 2.26.8. The public exploit claim comes from X and is unverified. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p34x-fmph-9fjx

ASUS Control Center Express (Nov 19): hard-coded key flaws incl. CVE-2026-114202 (CVSS 10) let a remote unauthenticated attacker forge tokens and take over the console and managed PCs. Update to 1.7.29 and update client agents.
Unverified (X): Qilin claims ransomware at Osaki Electric (Japan) that halted smart-meter production and shipments.

Splunk November advisories (Nov 18): SOAR App Wizard RCE CVE-2026-131253 (CVSS 9.9, authenticated; fix SOAR 8.8.0), Enterprise Security path-traversal RCE CVE-2026-131202 (ess_admin; fix 8.7.0), Enterprise RapidDiag CVE-2026-76535 (9.1; fixed 10.6.1/10.4.5/10.2.9/10.0.12/9.4.17).
